title: sister_used_my_wedding_fund
beats: My sister (31F) asked to borrow $4,000 'for two weeks' back in March, and I (28F) said yes because that's what family does.
I'd been saving that money quietly for almost two years, a little from every paycheck, for a wedding my boyfriend didn't even know I was planning around.
Two weeks turned into two months, then she stopped answering texts about it entirely.
I finally cornered her at our mom's birthday dinner and asked, calmly, when I'd see the money again.
She laughed and said 'it's not that deep, you're not even engaged yet,' in front of the whole table.
Turns out she hadn't just spent it slowly, she'd put it as a down payment on a car she'd already been driving for a month.
I asked to see the title. My name was nowhere on it, obviously, but neither was the loan she claimed she needed the cash for.
She'd lied about why she needed it in the first place, there was no emergency, no medical bill, just a car she wanted and couldn't afford alone.
I told her flat out I wanted my $4,000 back within 30 days or I was done being quiet about it to the family.
My mom pulled me aside and said I was 'materializing' a rift over money when 'she's your sister, she'd do it for you.'
My dad texted me later saying I 'humiliated' her at dinner and I should've handled it privately.
Here's the thing though: I'd asked her privately four separate times over two months before that dinner.
Now she's telling cousins I 'ambushed' her, and my mom wants me to apologize first to 'keep the peace.'
I blocked my sister on everything and told my parents I'm not attending Thanksgiving if she's centered as the victim.
My boyfriend, who I finally told everything to, says I did nothing wrong and the wedding fund explains why I've been quietly panicking for months.
My mom says I'm tearing the family apart over 'a car that's basically the same as cash anyway.'
